newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares up 2.31 pct at new record, off highs.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares up 2.31 pct at new record, off highs.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose further on Monday amid hopes that a newly formed secularist coalition would win a confidence vote in parliament in coming weeks, but fell from early highs on profit-taking.

The IMKB National-100 closed at an all-time high of 1,857, up 42 points, or 2.31 percent from Friday's previous record close of 1,815, but down from a trading record of 1,910 it brushed in the morning. It had soared 10.5 percent last week.
Trade volume jumped to 53.02 trillion lira from Friday's 49.52 trillion.

"Profit-taking which emerged after (President Suleyman) Demirel approved the new coalition was normal because the index had been rising since last week on expectations that the (secularist) government would be formed," said Korhan Bilecik from Deha securities.

Conservative opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz officially became the new prime minister when Demirel approved his cabinet list at midday. He physically took over the job from Islamist Necmettin Erbakan at a handing-over ceremony in the afternoon.

"I expect the index to continue its uptrend until the confidence vote, but with intermittent profit-taking. Technically, support is awaited at the index's 1,800-1,850 range and psychological resistance at 2,000," Bilecik said.
The programme to be prepared by Yilmaz's government is expected to be read in parliament next Monday, to be followed by a two-day debate and then a confidence vote expected on July 12.
Yilmaz's alliance is a minority coalition of two right and one left-wing parties, supported by another left-wing party.
Yilmaz said he expected to win the vote with a bigger-than-expected margin with the help of the latest defections from the alliance of former Islamist Erbakan and conservative Tansu Ciller.

Of the 246 shares traded, rises outdid falls by 148 to 53 and 45 were steady. The IMKB Industrial gained 2.19 percent to 1,729, the IMKB Services firmed 1.19 percent to 1,874 and the IMKB Financial jumped 3.5 percent to 2,011.

Actives were led by state flat steel maker Eregli, up 750 lira at 24,750, utilities Cukurova Elektrik, steady at 255,000 lira, Aktas Elektrik, up 10,000 lira at 265,000 and T.Isbank's C series, up 4,500 lira at 58,000. They made up 26.9 percent of the total turnover.
